notes: Two things. First, the cross-grades: the same measurement-tool limit as every earlier round. The pack's scope includes /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, which holds the C library; the tool's restore script empties each scope root before unpacking it, so tar cannot load: "/.securebench/harness/restore.sh: 9: tar: not found" (exit 127). N->S then reports failed/case_error ("adapter exited with status 1"), and N->s->N and S->N end in RewardFileNotFoundError. N passed; N->S says nothing about SecureBench and should be counted as not run. Second, S failed/oracle on its own, where earlier rounds passed: "no debian directory" in pmars-0.9.4. The SecureBench agent found dpkg-source missing, untarred pmars_0.9.4.orig.tar.xz and pmars_0.9.4-1.debian.tar.xz by hand in /app, and applied the Debian patches. The Debian tarball unpacks to /app/debian, not /app/pmars-0.9.4/debian (its candidate holds app/debian/changelog, app/debian/rules and so on). Upstream's test_debian_source_used checks `source_dirs[0] / "debian"` under /app/pmars-*, so the native grader would fail this too. SecureBench's verdict is correct; S->N could not confirm it because of the same tar limit.
